brief: A three-storey tower: drawers on the bottom storey and open bins on the top storey.

requirements.evidence: Stacked cells at q0,r0 across level 0,1,2 (piece:0,0,0;full + piece:0,0,1;full + piece:0,0,2;full) plus adjacent top cell at 0,1,2 gives three levels of structure, verified by get_build and 20 caps/joints locked.
4 drawers serving level 0: three notch drawers notch:0#-1,1#notch0, notch:0#0,-1#notch4, notch:0#1,-1#notch4 and one cut-face drawer drawer:0#1,0#cut on half-n base at 1,0,0.
Two open bins on level 2: bin:0,0,2~hex-bin-full (central tower top) and bin:0,1,2~hex-bin-full (adjacent top cell), both uncapped top openings.

finish.summary: Built a 3-level tower (0,0,0-2) with two additional bottom anchor cells for drawer frames. Bottom storey has 4 drawers (3 notch + 1 half-base drawer). Top storey has 2 open full-depth bins. Capped open faces and locked joints, meshClash clear.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
